header.name: Prototyping Interactive Systems
header.description: Introduction to Engineering Design is a multidisciplinary course offered with an aim to ignite your mind with concepts in design and innovation as well as engineering skills needed to build physical prototypes. This hands-on learning course is divided into 3 parts: In the first part, you will learn to work with microcontrollers, smartphones, low- cost materials, and power tools through several in-class activities and lab exercises. In the second part, you will apply these skills to a two-week long minor group project for a given design brief. The last part of the course is dedicated to the realization of an open- ended major group project. For this project, you will identify a problem, preferably having a social impact, plan your project and, finally, build a functional solution. The course culminates with a public showcase of the final prototypes.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: You will learn different methods of interacting with computers including command line, GUI, and novel sensors and actuators.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: You will be able to plan, design and develop prototypes of interactive systems including its form, function, and interface.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: You will be able to identify important components of a PC and how they are connected.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: You will learn to document and share your projects through self- made websites and posters.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: You will be able to identify electronic components, and procure them.
